domain: Device and system state telemetry (iOS 26 shipping / iOS 27 beta 4, July 2026) — self-installed sideloaded quantified-self app, free Apple ID

capabilities.api: UIDevice.current.isBatteryMonitoringEnabled = true; UIDevice.current.batteryLevel (Float 0.0–1.0, -1.0 if monitoring off); UIDevice.batteryLevelDidChangeNotification (UIDeviceBatteryLevelDidChangeNotification); typed msg UIDevice.BatteryLevelDidChangeMessage
capabilities.permission: none — no Info.plist key, no prompt
capabilities.resolution: CONTESTED. Rounded to nearest 0.05 (5%) since iOS 17; was 1% on iOS 16 and earlier. Widely reported as a regression on the Apple forums (threads 738140, 732903, 774241, 788911); Apple has not documented the change. Notification fires per 5% step, so ~20 events per full discharge.
capabilities.backfill: none — no historical store; you must sample and persist
capabilities.notes: isBatteryMonitoringEnabled must be set true or you get -1.0; the flag does not persist across launches — set it in didFinishLaunching. The PROPERTY is readable on any background wake (BGAppRefreshTask, location callback, audio session); the NOTIFICATION is only delivered to a live process. Screen-time-correlated discharge rate is the interesting derived metric and needs continuous background execution to be meaningful.

capabilities.resolution: Event-driven, exact transitions; 4 discrete states. No distinction between wired, MagSafe, and Qi charging; no wattage; no charge-cycle count.
capabilities.notes: Also requires isBatteryMonitoringEnabled. This is the single best sleep-window proxy in the whole domain: plug-in time + Low Power Mode + zero foreground lifecycle events for N hours brackets sleep without any HealthKit permission.

Note the notification name is the legacy NSProcessInfoPowerStateDidChange — it is NOT spelled powerStateDidChangeNotification. Auto-enables at 20% and 10%, so it doubles as a coarse battery-threshold signal even without battery monitoring. Auto-disables at 80% when charging.

capabilities.resolution: 4 discrete levels, event-driven. No numeric temperature is exposed by any public API — no CPU temp, no battery temp.
capabilities.notes: A strong proxy for heavy use, charging, direct sun, or being in a pocket/car. Correlating .serious with battery drain rate and screen-on time is the highest-signal derived metric here.

capabilities.stream: Apple Watch battery level and charging state
capabilities.api: WKInterfaceDevice.current().isBatteryMonitoringEnabled = true; .batteryLevel; .batteryState → WKInterfaceDeviceBatteryState; relay to phone via WatchConnectivity WCSession.transferUserInfo / updateApplicationContext
capabilities.resolution: Same 5%-ish granularity semantics as iOS; watchOS background refresh budget is tighter than iOS.
capabilities.notes: Requires shipping a separate watchOS target. On a free Apple ID this consumes a second slot against the 3-app limit and expires on the same 7-day clock. WKInterfaceDevice also exposes wristLocation, crownOrientation, waterResistanceRating, isWaterLockEnabled, supportsAudioStreaming, screenBounds, screenScale, preferredContentSizeCategory, layoutDirection, identifierForVendor, systemName, systemVersion, name, model, localizedModel.

capabilities.resolution: Static integer; activeProcessorCount can drop as the system parks cores under thermal pressure — sampling it alongside thermalState gives a free throttling signal
capabilities.notes: activeProcessorCount is the only public window into core parking. There is no public API for CPU load percentage of your own process or the system — host_processor_info / task_info are Mach APIs that work on a sideloaded build but are undocumented and unreliable for whole-system load.
Device-model fingerprint, not a time series. Combined with processorCount and UIScreen.nativeBounds it identifies the exact iPhone model without any private API.

capabilities.stream: Memory headroom available to your app
capabilities.resolution: Exact bytes at call time. Returns (current dirty-memory limit − current dirty footprint), NOT free system RAM.
capabilities.notes: Apple explicitly warns the value is a snapshot and must not be cached — it can be invalidated instantly by another thread or framework. The limit itself changes across the app lifecycle (background limits are far lower than foreground), so this is really a measure of your own pressure, not the device's. Pair with UIApplication.didReceiveMemoryWarningNotification.
DispatchSource memory-pressure is the system-wide signal and fires even when your app is not the cause; the UIApplication notification is your-process-scoped. Both only reach a running process.

capabilities.api: URL.resourceValues(forKeys:) with .volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey (Int64), .volumeAvailableCapacityForOpportunisticUsageKey (Int64), .volumeAvailableCapacityKey (Int), .volumeTotalCapacityKey (Int). Also volumeIsInternal, volumeIsRemovable, volumeIsLocal, volumeIsReadOnly, volumeIsEjectable, volumeIsEncrypted, volumeIsJournaling, volumeIsRootFileSystem, volumeIsBrowsable, volumeIsAutomounted, volumeName, volumeLocalizedName, volumeTypeName, volumeLocalizedFormatDescription, volumeUUIDString, volumeIdentifier, volumeCreationDate, volumeResourceCount, volumeMaximumFileSize, volumeMountFromLocation, volumeSubtype, volumeURLForRemounting
capabilities.resolution: Exact bytes, poll-only — there is no disk-space change notification
capabilities.notes: TRAP: volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsage counts PURGEABLE space (caches iOS is willing to evict), so it routinely reports MORE than true free space and can exceed volumeAvailableCapacity. For a QS 'how full is my phone' series use volumeAvailableCapacity for the honest number and ImportantUsage for the number Settings shows. Also note this is a REQUIRED-REASON API for App Store distribution (NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryDiskSpace, codes 85F4.1 / E174.1 / 7D9E.1 / B728.1) — inert for sideloading, but it tells you Apple classifies disk space as a fingerprinting vector.

CONTESTED, and both sides are right. systemUptime counts only AWAKE time and iOS devices sleep constantly, so uptime deltas do not equal wall-clock deltas (Apple forums 101874, 98682). kern.boottime gives a wall-clock boot instant but is expressed relative to the CURRENT system clock, so it shifts whenever the clock is adjusted (NTP, timezone, manual). Apple DTS answered directly (forum 809339) that systemUptime + persistent storage is NOT a reliable restart detector: 'You could probably make it work a lot of the time, but it definitely won't be completely reliable.' Practical approach: persist BOTH on every sample and treat a boottime jump >2s that is NOT accompanied by a clock-change notification as a reboot. System boot time is also a required-reason API (NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategorySystemBootTime, code 35F9.1). sysctl on iOS is public but Apple declines to promise long-term binary compatibility.

capabilities.resolution: Continuous 0.0–1.0. Reflects the user/auto-brightness SLIDER position, not measured nits and not ambient light.
capabilities.notes: FOREGROUND-ONLY in practice. The notification is not delivered to a suspended app, and the value read on a background wake reflects the last foreground state rather than live screen state (the screen is usually off). Auto-Brightness moves this value, so as a QS stream it is a decent proxy for ambient light while the app is on screen. There is NO public ambient-light-sensor API on iOS; the only legitimate light proxy is the front camera (which needs NSCameraUsageDescription and is a different domain).

capabilities.api: iOS 26 and earlier: UIScreen.main.isCaptured + UIScreen.capturedDidChangeNotification (UIScreenCapturedDidChangeNotification). iOS 27: DEPRECATED → UITraitCollection.sceneCaptureState → UISceneCaptureState, observed via registerForTraitChanges(_:handler:)
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 11.0 (isCaptured); sceneCaptureState is the iOS 27 replacement
capabilities.notes: NEW IN iOS 27 — verified from the docs JSON: isCaptured is deprecated in iOS 27.0 / iPadOS 27.0 / tvOS 27.0 with the deprecation summary 'Use sceneCaptureState instead.' Write against sceneCaptureState with an availability fallback. Fires for QuickTime capture, screen recording, AirPlay mirroring, and (per Apple) Sidecar-style cloning. Tells you capture is happening, never what was captured.

capabilities.resolution: Event-driven, fires AFTER the screenshot is taken
capabilities.notes: HARD FOREGROUND-ONLY and the biggest expectation gap in this domain. You only learn about screenshots taken while YOUR app is on screen. Screenshots of Messages, Safari, or anything else are completely invisible — iOS will not wake you and there is no cross-app screenshot log. There is also no way to see the image or even its dimensions. (Photos/PHPhotoLibrary can retroactively enumerate screenshots via PHAssetMediaSubtype.photoScreenshot with photo-library permission — different domain, but it is the only real backfill path for screenshot history.)

capabilities.resolution: Mostly static; currentEDRHeadroom is dynamic and tracks HDR/brightness conditions
capabilities.notes: maximumFramesPerSecond distinguishes ProMotion (120) from non-ProMotion (60) hardware. currentEDRHeadroom is the closest thing to a live 'how bright is the panel actually running' signal. In iOS 27 the whole UIScreen surface is being pushed toward scene-based equivalents — prefer UIWindowScene.screen / traits for anything new.

TRAP: returns .unknown until you call beginGeneratingDeviceOrientationNotifications(); calls must be balanced with end… . Foreground-only. .faceDown is a genuinely useful QS signal (phone placed screen-down = deliberate disengagement). For true continuous attitude in the background use CoreMotion CMMotionManager.deviceMotion — permission-free, and it keeps running under a background mode.

capabilities.stream: Proximity sensor (phone held to ear / covered)
capabilities.notes: NOT passively usable. Enabling monitoring makes the system BLANK THE SCREEN whenever the sensor trips — the same behaviour as a phone call. You cannot silently log proximity while showing UI. Only enable it during an explicit 'pocket detection' mode the user opts into, and only iPhone has the sensor (isProximityMonitoringEnabled silently stays false on iPad).

capabilities.permission: none — output volume needs NO microphone permission
capabilities.resolution: Continuous 0.0–1.0; changes in 1/16 steps via hardware buttons
capabilities.notes: Apple's docs explicitly state 'You can observe changes to the value of this property by using Key-value observing' and do NOT require session activation for the read — though in practice activating a .playback/.ambient session makes KVO reliably fire. Confirmed permission-free: only recording needs AVAudioApplication.requestRecordPermission. If you hold an audio background mode this keeps reporting while backgrounded, which is why it is one of the few genuinely 'yes' background rows.

capabilities.stream: Audio route (AirPods / speaker / CarPlay connection events)
capabilities.api: AVAudioSession.sharedInstance().currentRoute → AVAudioSessionRouteDescription (.outputs → [AVAudioSessionPortDescription] with .portType, .portName, .uid, .channels); AVAudioSession.routeChangeNotification with AVAudioSessionRouteChangeReasonKey; port types AVAudioSession.Port.bluetoothA2DP/.bluetoothHFP/.bluetoothLE/.headphones/.builtInSpeaker/.builtInReceiver/.carAudio/.airPlay/.usbAudio/.HDMI
capabilities.notes: This is your ONLY window onto AirPods. portName gives the user-assigned name ('Zach's AirPods Pro'), which is a strong presence/context signal — AirPods connected + car audio route = driving. There is NO public AirPods battery API, no ear-detection API, and no head-tracking outside of CMHeadphoneMotionManager (which is CoreMotion, permission-free, and DOES report head orientation from AirPods Pro/Max — worth adding if you want that stream).

The closest sanctioned substitute for 'is the user consuming media right now'. It tells you SOMETHING with a non-mixable session is playing — never which app, never what content. interruptionNotification additionally reveals phone calls, Siri, and alarms as .began/.ended events, which is a real attention-interruption stream.

capabilities.resolution: Event-driven but LAGGY and lossy — see notes
capabilities.notes: CONTESTED — widely used as a lock proxy, and Apple DTS says that is wrong. Three concrete failure modes: (1) complete non-starter if the user has no passcode set, because protected data never becomes unavailable; (2) after an unlock, protected data stays available for roughly 10–40 seconds past re-lock, so you get delayed and missing edges; (3) it measures data-protection class availability, which is not the same event as screen lock. Apple forums 751215 / 808006 carry the DTS position: 'there's no supported way to track the device lock state.' Usable as a COARSE screen-off signal with explicit error bars; not usable as a precise lock timestamp.

capabilities.stream: Scene-level system authentication protection (Face ID app lock)
capabilities.notes: Frequently mistaken for a lock-state API. It is NOT. It reports whether the SYSTEM is gating this scene behind Face ID/Touch ID (the iOS 18 'Require Face ID' per-app lock / Hidden apps feature), so it tells you about your own app's protection state, not the device screen lock. Apple's stated use case: 'You may want to disable your own app's privacy shielding if the system already requires authentication.' Include it for completeness; do not build a lock-state series on it.

capabilities.api: UIApplication.shared.applicationState → UIApplication.State {.active, .inactive, .background}; notifications didFinishLaunchingNotification, didBecomeActiveNotification, willResignActiveNotification, didEnterBackgroundNotification, willEnterForegroundNotification, willTerminateNotification, significantTimeChangeNotification; typed msgs UIApplication.DidBecomeActiveMessage / WillResignActiveMessage / DidEnterBackgroundMessage / WillEnterForegroundMessage / DidFinishLaunchingMessage / WillTerminateMessage / SignificantTimeChangeMessage
capabilities.notes: Measures attention to YOUR app only — it is not screen-time and gives you nothing about other apps. willResignActive additionally fires for transient interruptions (incoming call, Control Centre pull-down, notification banner tap), so an active→inactive→active cycle with no background transition is an interruption signature. Note significantTimeChangeNotification fires at midnight, on carrier time updates, and on DST transitions — useful as a free daily rollover trigger.

capabilities.stream: Scene activation state (per-window attention, multi-window on iPad)
capabilities.api: UIScene.activationState → UIScene.ActivationState {.unattached, .foregroundActive, .foregroundInactive, .background}; UIScene.willConnectNotification, didDisconnectNotification, didActivateNotification, willDeactivateNotification, willEnterForegroundNotification, didEnterBackgroundNotification; UIApplication.shared.connectedScenes; UISceneSession
capabilities.notes: NEW/BREAKING IN iOS 27, verified from Apple's UIKit updates page: 'Starting in iOS 27, apps built with the latest SDK must use the scene-based life cycle or they fail to launch.' Build the app scene-based from day one and record scene events rather than UIApplication ones. On iPad this is strictly richer than UIApplication.applicationState because it distinguishes Split View / Stage Manager windows.

capabilities.api: UIAccessibility.isVoiceOverRunning, isSwitchControlRunning, isAssistiveTouchRunning, isVideoAutoplayEnabled, isBoldTextEnabled, buttonShapesEnabled, isClosedCaptioningEnabled, shouldDifferentiateWithoutColor, isGrayscaleEnabled, isDarkerSystemColorsEnabled, isInvertColorsEnabled, isMonoAudioEnabled, isOnOffSwitchLabelsEnabled, isReduceMotionEnabled, isReduceTransparencyEnabled, isShakeToUndoEnabled, isSpeakScreenEnabled, isSpeakSelectionEnabled, prefersCrossFadeTransitions, isGuidedAccessEnabled; plus UIAccessibility.hearingDevicePairedEar and guidedAccessRestrictionState(forIdentifier:)
capabilities.notes: isGuidedAccessEnabled is the standout QS signal — Guided Access is a deliberate focus/lock-in action by the user. The ObjC constant names differ from the Swift ones in two cases worth knowing: isDarkerSystemColorsEnabled maps to UIAccessibilityDarkerSystemColorsEnabled (no 'Is'), and shouldDifferentiateWithoutColor maps to UIAccessibilityShouldDifferentiateWithoutColor.

capabilities.stream: Accessibility settings change events (full enumeration — 21 notifications)
capabilities.api: UIAccessibility.voiceOverStatusDidChangeNotification, switchControlStatusDidChangeNotification, assistiveTouchStatusDidChangeNotification, videoAutoplayStatusDidChangeNotification, boldTextStatusDidChangeNotification, buttonShapesEnabledStatusDidChangeNotification, closedCaptioningStatusDidChangeNotification, differentiateWithoutColorDidChangeNotification, grayscaleStatusDidChangeNotification, darkerSystemColorsStatusDidChangeNotification, invertColorsStatusDidChangeNotification, monoAudioStatusDidChangeNotification, onOffSwitchLabelsDidChangeNotification, reduceMotionStatusDidChangeNotification, reduceTransparencyStatusDidChangeNotification, shakeToUndoDidChangeNotification, speakScreenStatusDidChangeNotification, speakSelectionStatusDidChangeNotification, prefersCrossFadeTransitionsStatusDidChange, guidedAccessStatusDidChangeNotification, hearingDevicePairedEarDidChangeNotification
capabilities.notes: Note the naming inconsistency Apple never cleaned up: prefersCrossFadeTransitionsStatusDidChange has NO 'Notification' suffix in Swift, unlike all 20 siblings. Delivered only to a live process — poll the properties on background wake instead.

capabilities.stream: UI traits fingerprint (dark mode, text size, contrast, layout)
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 8.0 base; sceneCaptureState iOS 27; systemPrefersReducedResourceUsage iOS 27 (beta)
capabilities.resolution: Discrete enums, event-driven while a view hierarchy is live
capabilities.notes: userInterfaceStyle is a genuine circadian signal if the user runs Appearance on the sunrise/sunset automatic schedule — the light→dark flip timestamps are a free daylight proxy. preferredContentSizeCategory changes are rare but high-signal (fatigue, eye strain). Traits require a live trait environment (view/window/scene), so this whole row is foreground-only; cache last-known values for background reporting.

GENUINELY NEW — verified from the iOS 27 beta docs. Apple's discussion verbatim: 'When this value is YES, the system has entered a state where it would prefer apps to scale back resource-intensive work.' This is a broader, earlier-firing distress signal than thermalState or Low Power Mode and appears to aggregate thermal, power, and memory pressure. Log all three together — the divergence between them is itself the interesting series. Still beta; the symbol may change before September GA.

A permission-FREE travel and jet-lag detector — no location permission needed, and it is the only geographic signal in this entire domain. Cache TimeZone.current.identifier and TimeZone.current.secondsFromGMT() on every sample. Note that TimeZone.current is snapshotted at first access; use autoupdatingCurrent or re-read after the notification.

Very low event rate — this is a fingerprint/config field, not a time series. Worth capturing once per session. Note the active-keyboard list (UITextInputMode.activeInputModes) is a much richer language fingerprint but is a required-reason API (NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryActiveKeyboards) for App Store distribution.

capabilities.stream: Network path: interface type, expensive/constrained, connectivity
capabilities.permission: none — this is NOT the gated 'Access WiFi Information' capability
capabilities.minIOS: iOS 12.0; isUltraConstrained and linkQuality are iOS 26.0
capabilities.resolution: Event-driven on every path change; sub-second
capabilities.notes: NEW IN iOS 26 (verified from docs JSON): NWPath.linkQuality — 'Represents the link quality measurement of the link layer network attachment', with Apple's caveat 'Do not use this value to gate connection attempts'; and NWPath.isUltraConstrained — 'Checks if the path uses an NWInterface that is considered to be constrained by user preference'. isExpensive ≈ on cellular/hotspot; isConstrained ≈ Low Data Mode. Wi-Fi vs cellular transitions are an excellent free home/away/commute proxy WITHOUT location permission. Reading the actual SSID is a different thing and DOES need the Access WiFi Information capability, which a free Apple ID cannot sign.

capabilities.stream: Cellular radio technology and SIM presence
capabilities.entitlement: none for radio tech; 'SIM Inserted for Wireless Carriers' capability is a separate gated thing
capabilities.notes: DEPRECATION TRAP: CTCarrier and serviceSubscriberCellularProviders were deprecated in iOS 16 with NO replacement, and on current iOS they return dummy placeholder values ('--', mcc '65535'). Do not build anything on carrier name or MCC/MNC. serviceCurrentRadioAccessTechnology still works and 5G-NR vs LTE vs no-service is a usable coverage/location-context signal. Note NWPathMonitor is the better-supported modern path for almost everything here.

capabilities.stream: Your own app's delivered notifications and notification settings
capabilities.api: UNUserNotificationCenter.current().getDeliveredNotifications(completionHandler:) → [UNNotification]; .getPendingNotificationRequests(completionHandler:); .getNotificationSettings(completionHandler:) → UNNotificationSettings (authorizationStatus, alertSetting, badgeSetting, soundSetting, lockScreenSetting, notificationCenterSetting, criticalAlertSetting, timeSensitiveSetting, scheduledDeliverySetting, alertStyle, showPreviewsSetting, providesAppNotificationSettings, announcementSetting, directMessagesSetting); .removeDeliveredNotifications(withIdentifiers:); .removeAllDeliveredNotifications()
capabilities.permission: Only if you post notifications: UNUserNotificationCenter.requestAuthorization(options:) prompts. Reading getNotificationSettings needs no prompt. No Info.plist key.
capabilities.resolution: Exact per-notification records with date and content — but ONLY yours
capabilities.notes: CONFIRMED: own-app only. Apple's own wording is 'Fetches all of YOUR APP'S delivered notifications that are still present in Notification Center', and current() 'Returns YOUR APP'S notification center.' There is no public cross-app notification read on iOS at any entitlement tier — see blockers. getNotificationSettings is quietly the more interesting row for QS: scheduledDeliverySetting reveals Scheduled Summary is on, timeSensitiveSetting and criticalAlertSetting reveal the user's interruption tolerance, and none of it needs a prompt.

capabilities.permission: none to READ; the user controls the setting in Settings
capabilities.entitlement: none (Background Modes capability IS available on a free Apple ID)
capabilities.notes: Log this as a DATA-QUALITY channel, not a QS signal. When it flips to .denied your entire partial-background tier silently dies, and without this row you would misread the resulting gap as 'the user did nothing'. Every longitudinal series in this domain should carry a companion 'was collection actually possible' flag.

capabilities.api: BGTaskScheduler.shared.register(forTaskWithIdentifier:using:launchHandler:); BGAppRefreshTaskRequest; BGProcessingTaskRequest (requiresNetworkConnectivity, requiresExternalPower); BGContinuedProcessingTaskRequest (iOS 26); Info.plist BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers + UIBackgroundModes
capabilities.entitlement: Background Modes capability, which IS available to a free Apple ID. GPU access for BGContinuedProcessingTask needs com.apple.developer.background-tasks.continued-processing.gpu (paid).
capabilities.resolution: BGAppRefreshTask ≈30s, opportunistic, no cadence guarantee. BGProcessingTask runs longer but typically only when charging and idle.
capabilities.notes: NEW IN iOS 26: BGContinuedProcessingTask — 'A task that starts in the foreground and can continue running in the background as needed.' Apple: 'The system displays the progress of this task in a Live Activity and a person can cancel it through the interface.' It is user-visible and cancellable, and the system 'prioritizes the termination of tasks that reflect minimal or no progress' — so it is for finite user-initiated jobs, NOT a silent always-on sampler. The real always-on lever is still a location or audio background mode. CRITICAL: all BGTaskScheduler wakes stop permanently if the user force-quits the app from the app switcher, and never resume until the app is manually relaunched.

capabilities.stream: Device model / OS version identity fingerprint
capabilities.api: UIDevice.current.systemName, .systemVersion, .model, .localizedModel, .userInterfaceIdiom, .identifierForVendor, .isMultitaskingSupported, .name; ProcessInfo.processInfo.operatingSystemVersion, .operatingSystemVersionString, .isOperatingSystemAtLeast(_:), .hostName, .processName, .processIdentifier, .globallyUniqueString, .arguments, .environment, .isMacCatalystApp, .isiOSAppOnMac; uname()/sysctlbyname("hw.machine") for the raw model code (e.g. iPhone17,1)
capabilities.entitlement: none for everything except UIDevice.name — see notes
capabilities.notes: TRAP: since iOS 16, UIDevice.current.name returns a GENERIC string ('iPhone', 'iPad') unless you hold com.apple.developer.device-information.user-assigned-device-name, which is a special-request entitlement Apple grants case-by-case and which a free Apple ID cannot sign. UIDevice.model is also useless ('iPhone') — use sysctlbyname('hw.machine') for the real model code. identifierForVendor resets when all apps from the same vendor are uninstalled, so it is not a durable device key for a QS log; generate your own UUID and store it in the Keychain (Keychain Sharing IS free-tier).

capabilities.stream: Device performance-tier probes (symbols present, docs unretrievable)
capabilities.notes: AUDITABLE NEGATIVE: both symbols are present in the live ProcessInfo documentation JSON I pulled, but their dedicated doc pages returned HTTP 404 and web search surfaced no substantive coverage. NSDeviceCertification appears to relate to the iOS 17 high-performance-gaming device tier; NSProcessPerformanceProfile appears related to the Sustained Execution capability (which is PAID-tier only per Apple's capability table). Listed for completeness — availability and semantics UNVERIFIED. Do not build on these without checking the SDK headers directly.

blockers: FREE APPLE ID 7-DAY EXPIRY — the project-killer, and it is not an API problem. A Personal Team provisioning profile expires 7 days after creation. A quantified-self logger that dies every week and must be re-signed and re-installed from Xcode is a fundamentally different product from one that runs for a year. Compounding limits: max 3 free-provisioned apps installed on one device at a time (a companion watchOS app consumes a slot), and no TestFlight. Mitigations that actually work: (a) a weekly automated re-sign/re-deploy script driven by xcodebuild + devicectl, (b) AltStore/SideStore, which automates the 7-day refresh over Wi-Fi, or (c) pay the $99/yr Apple Developer Program, which extends profiles to 1 year and unlocks every blocked capability below. For a multi-month QS dataset, (c) is the honest recommendation.

INFocusStatusCenter (Focus mode) IS BLOCKED ON A FREE APPLE ID. This is the single most consequential finding and it contradicts most online write-ups. Reading Focus status needs three things: NSFocusStatusUsageDescription in Info.plist, INFocusStatusCenter.default.requestAuthorization, AND the Communication Notifications capability (entitlement com.apple.developer.usernotifications.communication). I pulled the raw HTML of Apple's own capability matrix at developer.apple.com/support/app-capabilities/ (the rendered checkmarks are <figure class="icon icon-checksolid"> elements that summarizers routinely hallucinate) and the row reads: Communication Notifications — ADP yes, ADEP yes, free Apple Developer NO. Without the capability, requestAuthorization returns denied. Free tier gets exactly 9 capabilities: App groups, Background modes, Data protection, HealthKit, HomeKit, Inter-App Audio, Keychain sharing, Maps, Wireless Accessory Configuration.

Even WITH the paid entitlement, Focus status is nearly useless for QS. INFocusStatus exposes a single optional Bool, isFocused. You learn that SOME Focus is active. You never learn WHICH one — Sleep vs Work vs Personal vs Do Not Disturb vs Driving are indistinguishable, and there is no schedule, no start time, and no way to enumerate configured Focus modes. Do Not Disturb specifically cannot be separated from any other Focus.

DeviceActivity / FamilyControls (per-app screen time — the highest-value device-state stream by far) IS BLOCKED ON A FREE APPLE ID. Apple's capability table shows 'Family Controls (development)' as ADP-only: not available to ADEP, not available to free. Apple DTS states plainly there is no supported way to use capabilities absent from the free-provisioning table. Even on a paid account, DISTRIBUTION requires a separate per-bundle-ID application form to Apple with a genuine parental-control or digital-wellbeing justification, and a separate request for every extension bundle ID (DeviceActivityMonitor, DeviceActivityReport, ShieldAction, ShieldConfiguration). Development-only use on a paid account works locally without approval. Net: per-app screen time requires $99/yr minimum.

NO CROSS-APP NOTIFICATION ACCESS EXISTS AT ANY TIER. UNUserNotificationCenter.current() is explicitly scoped to your app ('Returns your app's notification center'), and getDeliveredNotifications returns 'all of your app's delivered notifications'. There is no entitlement, private or public, that grants an iOS app read access to other apps' notifications. The ONE genuine exception is architectural, not an entitlement — see nonObvious re ANCS.

NO PUBLIC RING/SILENT SWITCH API — never has been, still none in iOS 26 or the iOS 27 betas. The only technique is the timing hack: play a ~0.5s silent system sound via AudioServicesPlaySystemSound and measure the completion-callback latency; under ~0.1s implies muted. CONTESTED and I could not verify it: the maintained libraries (akramhussein/Mute, GwynDurbridge/GDSilentDetector, Cap-go/capacitor-mute) still ship it, but their READMEs carry no iOS 17/18/26 compatibility statement and I found no post-iOS-17 confirmation that it still discriminates. Treat as unverified on iOS 26. It also cannot run in the background and it burns an audio session. The sanctioned partial replacement is Focus status, which is itself blocked on a free Apple ID.

DARWIN com.apple.springboard.lockstate / lockcomplete — DEAD FOR THIS USE CASE, and the App Store argument is the least important reason. Three separate findings: (1) UNDOCUMENTED — Apple's rule is that stringly-typed notification keys may only be used if listed in notify_keys.h, and neither key is; (2) APP STORE REJECTION is certain, with a specific rejection string ('Unsupported operation - Apps are not allowed to listen to device lock notifications'), which is IRRELEVANT to a sideloaded personal app; (3) THE ACTUAL KILLER — Apple DTS (Quinn 'The Eskimo!', forum thread 769398) states: 'iOS will not resume your app to receive a Darwin notification. If your app is suspended in the background when someone posts a notification... If your app is terminated while suspended, it will never receive the notification.' So even if SpringBoard still posts these keys on iOS 26 (which I could find no 2025–2026 confirmation of, only pre-iOS-17 code samples), a suspended logger receives nothing. The technique only works while you already hold continuous background execution — at which point you have better signals anyway. Note also Quinn's testing caveat: the Xcode debugger prevents suspension, so this appears to work in development and fails in the field.
NO NUMERIC TEMPERATURE, ANYWHERE. ProcessInfo.thermalState gives 4 buckets and that is the entire public thermal surface. No CPU temperature, no battery temperature, no ambient temperature.

NO BATTERY HEALTH, CYCLE COUNT, OR CHARGE WATTAGE. UIDevice.batteryState distinguishes 4 states and cannot tell wired from MagSafe from Qi. Battery health and cycle count (visible to the user in Settings) have no public API. Combined with the iOS 17 drop to 5% batteryLevel granularity, battery-based QS is coarser on iOS 26 than it was on iOS 15.

SCREENSHOT AND SCREEN-CAPTURE EVENTS ARE HARD FOREGROUND-ONLY. userDidTakeScreenshotNotification fires ONLY while your app is on screen; iOS will not wake you, and there is no cross-app screenshot log. isCaptured/sceneCaptureState likewise. Screenshots the user takes in Messages or Safari are permanently invisible to your app. This is the observable people most expect to work and it does not.
NO PUBLIC AMBIENT LIGHT SENSOR. UIScreen.brightness is the slider position, not lux. The only lux-ish path is the camera (different domain, needs NSCameraUsageDescription, cannot run backgrounded).

NO AIRPODS BATTERY API. Despite AirPods being in the hardware list, there is no public battery level for AirPods or any BLE accessory. AirPods surface only as AVAudioSession route port names/types plus CMHeadphoneMotionManager head orientation.

NO GENERAL SYSTEM CPU LOAD, PER-PROCESS LISTING, OR RUNNING-APP ENUMERATION. ProcessInfo.activeProcessorCount is the only public throttling hint. host_processor_info / sysctl KERN_PROC will link and run on a sideloaded build but are undocumented, sandbox-restricted in what they return, and Apple explicitly declines to promise binary compatibility.

CARRIER IDENTITY IS GONE. CTCarrier and serviceSubscriberCellularProviders were deprecated in iOS 16 with no replacement and now return placeholder values. Wi-Fi SSID requires the Access WiFi Information capability, which the free tier cannot sign.

NO PUSH NOTIFICATIONS ON A FREE APPLE ID. This removes silent-push (content-available) as a background wake mechanism, which is the standard trick for forcing periodic sampling. You are left with BGTaskScheduler (opportunistic, dies on force-quit) or a continuous background mode.

DEVICE LOCK STATE HAS NO SUPPORTED API AT ALL. Apple DTS, repeatedly: 'there's no supported way to track the device lock state.' Every available proxy is broken in a specific way — protectedData notifications need a passcode and lag 10–40s; UIScene.SystemProtectionManager reports per-app Face ID gating, not screen lock; Darwin notifications do not reach suspended apps. Screen-on/off time is genuinely NOT measurable by a third-party iOS app.
nonObvious: BACKGROUND MODES IS FREE-TIER — this single row makes the whole project viable, and it is the finding a competent dev would miss because everything else on the free tier is so restricted. Apple's capability table confirms 'Background modes: yes' for the free Apple Developer tier. Declaring UIBackgroundModes = location (with CLLocationManager.allowsBackgroundLocationUpdates = true and 'Always' authorization) or audio gives you a CONTINUOUSLY RUNNING PROCESS. Every 'partial' row in this answer silently promotes to 'yes' the moment you hold one: you can then poll battery, thermal, memory, disk, volume, and network on a timer forever, and every *DidChangeNotification actually reaches you. The audio-session variant (playing silence on a .playback session) is the classic trick and needs no location permission at all — but it seizes the audio route and will interrupt the user's music, so location is the better carrier for a QS logger. This inverts the usual advice: on a free Apple ID the background-execution question, not the permission question, determines data quality.

THE ENTIRE DOMAIN HAS ZERO BACKFILL. There is no historical store to query for any observable here — no battery history, no thermal log, no reboot log, no brightness history. Every series starts empty at first launch and exists only because your app sampled and persisted it. This is the opposite of HealthKit/CoreMotion, where years of data are waiting. It means (a) sampling cadence IS the data quality, (b) a 7-day-expiring free provisioning profile that interrupts collection is data loss, not inconvenience, and (c) you should over-sample early since you can never go back.

NOTIFICATION vs POLL IS THE UNIVERSAL RULE, and it answers the 'only observable while running' question uniformly. Apple DTS's Darwin answer generalizes to every NSNotification in this domain: a suspended app receives NOTHING, and if it is terminated while suspended it never receives the missed events at all. But the underlying PROPERTIES are process-local reads with no gate, so they are readable on any background wake. Therefore: batteryLevelDidChangeNotification, batteryStateDidChangeNotification, thermalStateDidChangeNotification, NSProcessInfoPowerStateDidChange, brightnessDidChangeNotification, capturedDidChangeNotification, userDidTakeScreenshotNotification, orientationDidChangeNotification, proximityStateDidChangeNotification, all 21 UIAccessibility change notifications, NSSystemTimeZoneDidChange, NSCurrentLocaleDidChange — all EVENT-LOSSY when backgrounded. Whereas batteryLevel, thermalState, isLowPowerModeEnabled, physicalMemory, os_proc_available_memory, disk capacities, NWPath.currentPath, TimeZone.current, and every UIAccessibility.is*Enabled property are POLLABLE on a background wake. Design consequence: never build on edge detection alone. Poll a full snapshot on every wake and reconstruct edges offline. HARD EXCEPTIONS that are foreground-only even when polled: UIScreen.brightness (screen is off), UITraitCollection (needs a live trait environment), UIDevice.orientation, proximityState, and anything screenshot/capture related.

ANCS IS THE ONE REAL PATH TO CROSS-APP NOTIFICATIONS, AND IT IS LEGITIMATE FOR A PERSONAL SETUP. The Apple Notification Center Service inverts the usual roles: the iPhone is the BLE *server* and a paired accessory is the *client*. Apple's own spec describes ANCS as giving 'Bluetooth accessories that connect to iOS devices... a simple and convenient way to access many kinds of notifications that are generated on iOS devices' — app identifier, title, message, date, category, for EVERY app. An iOS app acting as a CoreBluetooth central cannot consume its own device's ANCS. But a ~$5 ESP32 or nRF52 paired to the iPhone can subscribe to ANCS and log every notification, then hand the log back over BLE, Wi-Fi, or a file. For a self-installed personal QS rig where the owner is the subject, this is a clean, documented, no-entitlement route to the one stream iOS otherwise makes impossible. It is the highest-leverage idea in this answer.

THREE APIs IN THIS DOMAIN ARE FLAGGED BY APPLE AS FINGERPRINTING VECTORS, WHICH IS A ROADMAP TO WHAT IS ACTUALLY IDENTIFYING. The required-reason API list (privacy manifest, mandatory for App Store since May 1 2024) covers system boot time (NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategorySystemBootTime, reason 35F9.1), disk space (NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryDiskSpace, reasons 85F4.1 / E174.1 / 7D9E.1 / B728.1), active keyboards, file timestamps, and UserDefaults. This is entirely INERT for a sideloaded app — no privacy manifest is required and nothing is enforced at install. But it tells you which device-state signals Apple's own privacy team considers uniquely identifying, and boot time + free disk bytes + installed RAM + core count is indeed a near-unique device fingerprint. Worth knowing you are collecting it.

THREE GENUINELY NEW THINGS IN iOS 26/27 THAT CHANGE CODE YOU WOULD WRITE TODAY. (1) iOS 27 makes the scene-based lifecycle MANDATORY — Apple's UIKit updates page: 'Starting in iOS 27, apps built with the latest SDK must use the scene-based life cycle or they fail to launch.' Build scene-based now and record UIScene notifications rather than UIApplication ones. (2) UIScreen.isCaptured is DEPRECATED in iOS 27 in favour of UITraitCollection.sceneCaptureState. (3) NEW in iOS 27 beta: UIApplication.systemPrefersReducedResourceUsage + its notification and trait — a broader system-distress signal than thermalState or Low Power Mode. Also new in iOS 26: NWPath.linkQuality and NWPath.isUltraConstrained, and BGContinuedProcessingTask. iOS 27 is beta 4 as of 20 July 2026 (public beta 13 July, GA September), so the beta symbols may still change.

THE BEST SLEEP DETECTOR HERE NEEDS NO HEALTH PERMISSION AT ALL. Charging state + Low Power Mode + absence of foreground lifecycle events + screen brightness frozen + no orientation changes, sustained for N hours, brackets a sleep window with zero HealthKit access, zero location access, and zero prompts. Layer NSSystemTimeZoneDidChange on top and you get jet lag for free. For a QS app whose owner values not granting permissions, this is a surprisingly strong baseline.

activeProcessorCount IS A FREE THERMAL-THROTTLING DETECTOR. iOS parks CPU cores under sustained thermal load, so ProcessInfo.activeProcessorCount drops below processorCount before thermalState necessarily escalates. Sampling both, plus the iOS 27 systemPrefersReducedResourceUsage flag, gives three independent pressure signals — and the DIVERGENCE between them is more informative than any one of them.

AUTOMATIC DARK MODE IS A FREE DAYLIGHT SENSOR. If the user runs Appearance on the sunset-to-sunrise schedule, UITraitCollection.userInterfaceStyle flips at civil twilight. Logging those two timestamps per day gives you a daylight-hours series with no location permission — and combined with the timezone notification, it detects latitude changes from travel.

ALWAYS LOG A COLLECTION-VIABILITY CHANNEL ALONGSIDE THE DATA. UIApplication.backgroundRefreshStatus, whether a background mode is currently held, and the timestamp of the last successful wake should be persisted on every sample. Without them, a gap caused by the user force-quitting the app (which permanently stops all BGTaskScheduler wakes until manual relaunch) or toggling off Background App Refresh is indistinguishable from a gap caused by the user genuinely doing nothing. In a domain with zero backfill, silently misattributed gaps are the dominant failure mode.

UNNotificationSettings IS AN UNPROMPTED INTERRUPTION-TOLERANCE FINGERPRINT. getNotificationSettings requires no authorization prompt and returns scheduledDeliverySetting (Scheduled Summary on/off), timeSensitiveSetting, criticalAlertSetting, lockScreenSetting, notificationCenterSetting, showPreviewsSetting, announcementSetting and more. You cannot read other apps' notifications, but you CAN read how aggressively the user has configured their own interruption posture — and changes to it over time are a real behavioural signal.

DO NOT TRUST DOC-PAGE SUMMARIES FOR CAPABILITY/ENTITLEMENT QUESTIONS — FETCH THE RAW HTML. Apple's capability matrix renders availability as <figure class="icon icon-checksolid"> elements with no text content. A summarizing fetch of that page returned every capability as available to every tier, which is flatly wrong and would have put Focus Status in the wrong bucket and invalidated the free-Apple-ID conclusion. Raw HTML + a parser that keys on the icon class gives the truth. Relatedly, developer.apple.com documentation pages are client-rendered and return an empty shell to plain fetches — but the DocC JSON behind them at https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation/<path>.json returns the complete symbol list with exact identifiers, availability, and deprecation. That is how the full 20-property / 21-notification UIAccessibility enumeration and the iOS 27 isCaptured deprecation in this answer were obtained.
